note: Register of tabnas runtime dependencies that differ between this repository's ports (tabnas/admin ADR-24). tools/port-deps.cjs fails on a difference that is not listed here, and on an entry that no longer matches the manifests, so the list cannot outlive what it records. Every entry states the ports that have the dependency today, the reason, and the repair.

parser.reason: TypeScript: ts/src/xml.ts has `import { Tabnas } from '@tabnas/parser'`, a value import (`new Tabnas().use(jsonic).parse(grammarText)` in `Xml`), and a second import from the same package of `Rule`, `RuleSpec`, `Plugin`, `Context`, `Config`, `TabnasOptions` and `Lex`, all types; ts/package.json lists @tabnas/parser in peerDependencies. Rust: `use tabnas::...` in rs/src/lib.rs, lex.rs and namespace.rs, a call to `tabnas::GrammarSpec::from_value` and `pub use tabnas::TabnasError as XmlError` in lib.rs, with `tabnas` (package tabnas-parser) in [dependencies] of rs/Cargo.toml. Go: no .go file under go/, test files included, imports github.com/tabnas/parser/go, and go/go.mod carries the parser as `// indirect`. go/xml.go imports no tabnas module but github.com/tabnas/jsonic/go and constructs no engine: `Xml` builds its grammar as a `jsonic.GrammarSpec` literal and applies it with `j.Grammar` on the instance it is given, and every jsonic identifier it names (`jsonic.Jsonic`, `jsonic.Rule`, `jsonic.Context`, `jsonic.GrammarSpec`, `jsonic.Lex`, `jsonic.Token` among them) is an alias of an engine type, constant or variable declared in jsonic's go/engine.go. go/clib/core.go imports jsonic for jsonic's own function `Make` (`host.Make()`).
parser.repair: To agree on having it: go/xml.go would import github.com/tabnas/parser/go for the engine types, and the parser line in go/go.mod would become a direct require. Those aliases are all go/xml.go takes from jsonic, so moving every one of them would leave that file's jsonic import unused; jsonic would remain a dependency of the Go module through `host.Make` in go/clib/core.go. To agree on not having it: ts/src/xml.ts would take `Tabnas`, and the types `Rule`, `RuleSpec`, `Context`, `Config` and `Lex`, from @tabnas/jsonic, which re-exports them under the same names (jsonic's ts/src/jsonic.ts), `TabnasOptions` under the name `Options` (jsonic's ts/src/types.ts), and the engine's `Plugin` under the name `TabnasPlugin` (`export type { Plugin as TabnasPlugin } from '@tabnas/parser'`), because jsonic's own `Plugin` type is a different one whose first argument is a `Jsonic` instance; ts/package.json would then drop the @tabnas/parser peer. In Rust that move is not available today: tabnas-jsonic re-exports only `TabnasError` (as `JsonicError`), so jsonic's rs/src/lib.rs would first have to re-export the engine's items before rs/src here could take them from it and rs/Cargo.toml drop `tabnas` from [dependencies]. Either way the engine stays in every port's build, because jsonic depends on it in all three (peerDependencies of its ts/package.json, the import in its go/engine.go, [dependencies] of its rs/Cargo.toml). The handover page parser/doc/handover/README.md of 2026-10-04 does not raise this difference, but item 3 of its "Decisions waiting on the maintainer" proposes trying `use(json)` in place of `use(jsonic)` in xml: that edits the same `new Tabnas().use(jsonic)` call, and the second direction relies on @tabnas/jsonic remaining a dependency of the TypeScript port. Undecided: awaits the maintainer's ruling.
